Maladaptive Strategies.value: Being reminded of the event by others
I release my tension with sexual fantasies/ activities
Being around people in authority or uniform

Threat.value: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
I constantly scan my surroundings for signs of danger

Memory.value: My memories of the event feel more real and vivid than memories of ordinary things
I can taste what I tasted during the event when the memory returns
My memories of the event come in disconnected pieces that do not fit together

Negative Appraisals.value: If I think about the event, I will not be able to handle it
I have to be on guard all the time

vignette: Samantha, a 22-year-old South Eastern Asian woman, is a call center agent married to her college sweetheart. Her life took a drastic turn when she experienced a sexual assault six months ago while walking home from work late one evening. Since then, Samantha has struggled with a range of distressing symptoms that have significantly impacted her daily functioning and relationships. The traumatic event occurred on a dark street corner near her apartment complex. She was walking alone after finishing a long shift at the call center when she was attacked by an assailant who had been lurking in the shadows. The shock, fear, and pain of this assault remain vividly imprinted in Samantha’s mind, each memory feeling more real than any ordinary experience. The taste of the rain that fell during that night often returns to her palate whenever the memories resurface, making it nearly impossible for her to distinguish between past and present. Since then, Samantha has found herself reacting with intense fear at unexpected movements nearby, as if she is perpetually in danger. This hypervigilance extends to her constant scanning of exits as soon as she enters any room or building, a habit that she developed to ensure she can quickly escape should another threat arise. Her memories are fragmented and disconnected, making it difficult for her to form a coherent narrative of the event. One evening at home, Samantha heard an ambulance siren in the distance, which immediately triggered a flood of distressing thoughts and feelings related to her assault. The sound of sirens is now an almost unbearable reminder of that night, and she avoids areas where emergency vehicles are likely to be present. Additionally, stressful situations, such as a busy call center floor or family gatherings with happy families, have become increasingly difficult for her to endure. Samantha’s coping mechanisms have evolved over time. She frequently engages in sexual fantasies and activities to release tension, finding temporary relief from the overwhelming anxiety that haunts her daily life. However, she is deeply troubled by this behavior, as it makes her feel inadequate and further compounds her sense of inadequacy. Her avoidance behaviors have extended to authority figures and people in uniform, who remind her of the helplessness she felt during the assault. This has made interactions with coworkers in management positions at the call center particularly challenging. Samantha’s fear that thinking about the event will be too much for her to handle has led her to avoid conversations and reminders from others, even when it affects her relationships. Over time, these avoidance behaviors have taken a toll on her marriage. Her husband has noticed her withdrawal and occasional outbursts of anger but is unsure how to help or understand what she is going through. Samantha’s hypervigilance has also affected her work performance; she often finds herself distracted by scanning for potential threats in the call center, which can lead to errors and frustration from her supervisors. What finally brought Samantha to seek help was a recent incident at home when her husband tried to comfort her during an anxiety attack. His attempts were well-intentioned but inadvertently triggered more distress, highlighting the need for professional intervention. Samantha is most afraid of losing control and becoming overwhelmed by her thoughts and emotions. However, she is also hopeful that with proper support, she can regain a sense of safety and normalcy in her life. In this challenging period, Samantha hopes to find ways to manage her symptoms and build resilience against the overwhelming feelings of inadequacy and fear that have become so pervasive in her daily existence. Her journey towards recovery will require understanding, empathy, and targeted interventions aimed at addressing both her traumatic memories and her current coping mechanisms.
